The last sound is the consonant 'p'.
questions.explanation: The word 'cup' ends with the /p/ sound.

questions.stem: Which word has the short /i/ sound?
hints: Short /i/ sounds like 'i' in 'sit'.
Say each word and listen.
questions.explanation: 'Sit' has the short /i/ sound (/sɪt/). The other words have the long /aɪ/ or /iː/ sound.

questions.stem: In which word does the final 'y' make the /i/ sound?
hints: The /i/ sound is like 'ee' in 'see'.
In 'baby', the 'y' sounds like 'ee'.
questions.explanation: In 'baby', the final 'y' makes the /i/ sound. In 'fly', 'sky' and 'try', the final 'y' makes the /aɪ/ sound.

questions.stem: Which set of words all begin with the same consonant sound?
hints: Say each set aloud.
Which set has the same beginning sound in all three words?
questions.explanation: 'Jam', 'jug' and 'jet' all begin with the /dʒ/ sound.

questions.stem: Which word does NOT have a short vowel sound?
hints: Short vowels are /æ/, /e/, /ɪ/, /ɒ/, /ʌ/.
Which word has a long vowel sound?
questions.explanation: 'Cake' has the long /eɪ/ sound. The others have short vowel sounds.

questions.stem: Why is the 'k' silent in the word 'knee'?
options: Because 'kn' at the beginning of a word often has a silent 'k'
Because 'k' is never pronounced in English
Because the word is spelled wrong
hints: Think of other words starting with 'kn' — 'know', 'knife', 'knock'.
The 'k' is not pronounced in these words.
questions.explanation: In English, when 'k' comes before 'n' at the beginning of a word (kn-), the 'k' is usually silent.
misconceptions: 'K' is a consonant, not a vowel.
The spelling is correct; the 'k' is just silent.

questions.stem: Which word has the final 'y' making the /aɪ/ sound?
hints: /aɪ/ sounds like 'eye'.
In 'cry', the 'y' sounds like 'eye'.
questions.explanation: In 'cry', the final 'y' makes the /aɪ/ sound. In 'happy', 'baby' and 'puppy', the final 'y' makes the /i/ sound.

questions.stem: Which word ends with the same sound as 'book'?
hints: 'Book' ends with /k/.
Which word also ends with /k/?
questions.explanation: Both 'book' and 'look' end with the /k/ sound.

questions.stem: Which word has TWO silent letters?
hints: Look for a word where two letters are not pronounced.
In 'knife', the 'k' and the 'e' are silent.
questions.explanation: In 'knife', the 'k' is silent and the final 'e' is also silent (it makes the 'i' long).

questions.stem: Which word has a different short vowel sound from the others?
hints: Say each word and listen to the vowel.
'Hot', 'pot' and 'got' have the same vowel sound.
questions.explanation: 'Hot', 'pot' and 'got' have the short /ɒ/ sound. 'Hit' has the short /ɪ/ sound.
misconceptions: 'Hot', 'pot' and 'got' all have the same vowel.

questions.stem: In which word does the 'y' act as a consonant?
hints: A consonant 'y' makes the /j/ sound.
In 'yellow', the 'y' sounds like /j/.
questions.explanation: In 'yellow', the 'y' is a consonant making the /j/ sound. In 'happy', 'baby' and 'cry', the 'y' acts as a vowel.

indicator.subject: English Language
indicator.content_standard: B4.2.2.1: Connect sounds to letters; and blend letters/syllables in order to read and write
indicator.objective: Use words with consonant digraphs to make meaningful sentences

skills.description: Recognise consonant digraphs (sh, ch, ck, th, ph, wh, ng) in words
Read words containing consonant digraphs correctly
Use words with consonant digraphs to form meaningful sentences

spec.difficultyPlan: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4
misconceptions: A digraph is two separate sounds
Any two consonants make a digraph
Digraphs are only at the beginning of words
The letters in a digraph are pronounced separately

questions.stem: Which word contains the digraph 'sh'?
hints: The digraph 'sh' makes one sound (/ʃ/).
Say 'ship' slowly — you hear /ʃ/ at the beginning.
questions.explanation: 'Ship' contains the digraph 'sh', which makes the /ʃ/ sound.

questions.stem: Which word contains the digraph 'ch'?
hints: The digraph 'ch' makes one sound (/tʃ/).
Say 'chair' slowly — you hear /tʃ/ at the beginning.
questions.explanation: 'Chair' contains the digraph 'ch', which makes the /tʃ/ sound.

questions.stem: What sound does the digraph 'ck' make in the word 'duck'?
hints: 'Duck' ends with the /k/ sound.
The 'ck' digraph makes the /k/ sound.
questions.explanation: The digraph 'ck' makes the /k/ sound, as in 'duck'.

questions.stem: Which word contains the digraph 'th'?
hints: The digraph 'th' makes one sound (/θ/ or /ð/).
Say 'thin' slowly — you hear /θ/ at the beginning.
questions.explanation: 'Thin' contains the digraph 'th', which makes the /θ/ sound.

questions.stem: Which word does NOT contain a consonant digraph?
hints: A digraph is two consonants that make one sound.
'Ship', 'chair' and 'thin' all have digraphs.
questions.explanation: 'Cat' does not contain a digraph — 'c' and 't' are separate sounds. 'Ship' has 'sh', 'chair' has 'ch', 'thin' has 'th'.

questions.stem: What digraph is in the word 'phone'?
hints: The digraph 'ph' makes the /f/ sound.
Say 'phone' slowly — you hear /f/ at the beginning.
questions.explanation: 'Phone' contains the digraph 'ph', which makes the /f/ sound.

questions.stem: Which word contains the digraph 'wh'?
hints: The digraph 'wh' makes the /w/ sound (or /hw/ in some dialects).
Say 'whale' slowly — you hear /w/ at the beginning.
questions.explanation: 'Whale' contains the digraph 'wh', which makes the /w/ sound.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses a word with the digraph 'ch'?
hints: The digraph 'ch' is in 'child'.
Which sentence has a word with 'ch'?
questions.explanation: 'The child is playing' uses 'child', which contains the digraph 'ch'.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses a word with the digraph 'th'?
hints: The digraph 'th' is in 'weather'.
Which sentence has a word with 'th'?
questions.explanation: 'The weather is cold' uses 'weather', which contains the digraph 'th'.

questions.stem: Which word contains the digraph 'ng'?
hints: The digraph 'ng' makes the /ŋ/ sound.
Say 'ring' slowly — you hear /ŋ/ at the end.
questions.explanation: 'Ring' contains the digraph 'ng', which makes the /ŋ/ sound.

questions.stem: Which word contains a digraph at the END?
hints: Look for a word where the digraph is at the end, not the beginning.
'Fish' ends with 'sh'.
questions.explanation: 'Fish' ends with the digraph 'sh'. 'Ship', 'chair' and 'thin' have digraphs at the beginning.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses TWO words with consonant digraphs?
options: The chicken is in the kitchen.
hints: Look for a sentence with more than one word containing a digraph.
'Chicken' has 'ch' and 'ck'; 'kitchen' has 'ch'.
questions.explanation: 'The chicken is in the kitchen' uses 'chicken' (digraph 'ch' and 'ck') and 'kitchen' (digraph 'ch').
misconceptions: 'The cat is sleeping' has no digraphs.
'The dog is running' has no digraphs.
'The cup is red' has no digraphs.

questions.stem: Which set of words all contain the digraph 'th'?
hints: The digraph 'th' makes the /ð/ or /θ/ sound.
'This', 'that' and 'then' all have 'th'.
questions.explanation: 'This', 'that' and 'then' all contain the digraph 'th'.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses a word with the digraph 'wh'?
options: The whale is in the sea.
The cat is on the mat.
The dog is in the house.
The pen is on the table.
hints: The digraph 'wh' is in 'whale'.
Which sentence has a word with 'wh'?
questions.explanation: 'The whale is in the sea' uses 'whale', which contains the digraph 'wh'.

questions.stem: Which word contains a digraph and a blend?
hints: A blend has two consonant sounds; a digraph has two letters making one sound.
'Shrimp' has 'sh' (digraph) and 'r' (part of a blend 'shr').
questions.explanation: 'Shrimp' contains the digraph 'sh' and the blend 'shr' (sh + r).
misconceptions: 'Ship' has a digraph but no blend.
'Shop' has a digraph but no blend.
'Shut' has a digraph but no blend.

indicator.subject: English Language
indicator.content_standard: B4.2.2.2 [No separate content standard printed; continues from B4.2.2.1]
indicator.objective: Recognize and read words using a variety of cues (e.g. prefixes - word beginning)

skills.description: Recognise common prefixes (un-, re-, dis-, mis-, pre-) at the beginning of words
Identify the root word within a prefixed word
Understand how prefixes change meaning
Read unfamiliar words using prefix cues

spec.difficultyPlan: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4
misconceptions: A prefix is the main part of a word
A prefix changes the spelling of the root word
Prefixes can be added to any word

questions.stem: What is the prefix in the word 'unhappy'?
hints: A prefix is added at the beginning of a word.
In 'unhappy', 'un-' comes before 'happy'.
questions.explanation: The prefix in 'unhappy' is 'un-', which is added to the root word 'happy'.

questions.stem: Which of these words has a prefix?
hints: A prefix comes at the beginning.
'Re-' means 'again' in 'rewrite'.
questions.explanation: 'Rewrite' has the prefix 're-' (meaning 'again') added to the root 'write'.

questions.stem: What is the root word in 'disagree'?
hints: The root is the main part of the word without the prefix.
Remove 'dis-' from 'disagree'.
questions.explanation: The root word in 'disagree' is 'agree'. The prefix 'dis-' changes its meaning.
misconceptions: 'Dis' is the prefix, not the root.

questions.stem: What does the prefix 'un-' usually mean?
hints: Think of 'unhappy' — what does it mean?
'Un-' makes a word mean the opposite.
questions.explanation: The prefix 'un-' usually means 'not' or 'the opposite of' (e.g. unhappy = not happy).

questions.stem: Which word begins with the prefix 're-'?
hints: 'Re-' means 'again'.
'Return' means to come back again.
questions.explanation: 'Return' begins with the prefix 're-', meaning 'again' or 'back'.

questions.stem: What is the root word in 'preview'?
hints: Remove the prefix 'pre-' (meaning 'before').
What word is left?
questions.explanation: The root word in 'preview' is 'view'. The prefix 'pre-' means 'before'.

questions.stem: What does 'rewrite' mean?
hints: The prefix 're-' means 'again'.
So 'rewrite' means to write again.
questions.explanation: 'Rewrite' means to write again. The prefix 're-' adds the meaning 'again'.

questions.stem: What is the root word in 'misunderstand'?
hints: Remove the prefix 'mis-' (meaning 'wrongly').
What word is left?
questions.explanation: The root word in 'misunderstand' is 'understand'. The prefix 'mis-' means 'wrongly'.

questions.stem: What does 'prehistoric' mean?
hints: 'Pre-' means 'before'.
So 'prehistoric' means before written history.
questions.explanation: 'Prehistoric' means before history was written down. The prefix 'pre-' means 'before'.

questions.stem: Which word has the prefix 'dis-'?
hints: 'Dis-' means 'not' or 'opposite'.
'Dislike' means not to like.
questions.explanation: 'Dislike' has the prefix 'dis-' (meaning 'not') added to the root 'like'.
misconceptions: 'Distance' does not have a separate prefix 'dis-' in the same way.

questions.stem: If you know that 'un-' means 'not', what does 'unkind' mean?
hints: 'Un-' means 'not'.
So 'unkind' means not kind.
questions.explanation: 'Unkind' means not kind. The prefix 'un-' changes the meaning to its opposite.

questions.stem: If 're-' means 'again', what does 'replay' mean?
hints: 'Re-' means 'again'.
So 'replay' means to play again.
questions.explanation: 'Replay' means to play again. The prefix 're-' adds the meaning 'again'.

questions.stem: Which pair correctly shows the prefix and the root word in 'uncomfortable'?
hints: The prefix is 'un-' (meaning 'not').
The root word is 'comfortable'.
questions.explanation: In 'uncomfortable', the prefix is 'un-' (not) and the root word is 'comfortable'.
misconceptions: 'Comfort' is part of the root, but the full root is 'comfortable'.

questions.stem: A pupil reads the word 'misplace' for the first time. Using the prefix 'mis-' (wrongly), what does 'misplace' mean?
options: To put something in the wrong place
To put something in the right place
hints: 'Mis-' means 'wrongly'.
So 'misplace' means to place wrongly.
questions.explanation: 'Misplace' means to put something in the wrong place. The prefix 'mis-' adds the meaning 'wrongly'.

questions.stem: Which word means 'to not agree'?
hints: The prefix 'dis-' means 'not' or 'opposite'.
So 'disagree' means to not agree.
questions.explanation: 'Disagree' means to not agree. The prefix 'dis-' changes the meaning to the opposite.

questions.stem: Which word has a prefix that means 'before'?
hints: 'Pre-' means 'before'.
So 'prepay' means to pay before.
questions.explanation: 'Prepay' has the prefix 'pre-' meaning 'before'.

questions.stem: A pupil reads: 'The teacher asked us to rewrite our essays.' Using the prefix 're-', what does 'rewrite' mean in this sentence?
hints: 'Re-' means 'again'.
The teacher wants them to write again.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, 'rewrite' means to write the essays again. The prefix 're-' means 'again'.

questions.stem: Which word does NOT have a prefix?
hints: A prefix is added to a root word.
'Under' is a single word with no prefix.
questions.explanation: 'Under' does not have a prefix. 'Unhappy', 'rewrite' and 'preview' all have prefixes (un-, re-, pre-).

indicator.subject: English Language
indicator.content_standard: B4.2.4.1: Identify and use diphthongs to decode words
indicator.objective: Use closing diphthongs e.g. /ei/, /ai/, /oi/ to make meaningful sentences

skills.description: Recognise words containing target closing diphthongs (/ei/, /ai/, /oi/)
Identify which diphthong is heard in a given word
Use words with closing diphthongs to form meaningful sentences
Produce or select additional words containing a given diphthong

spec.difficultyPlan: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4
misconceptions: A diphthong is two separate vowel sounds said one after the other
The letter 'y' is never part of a diphthong
Diphthongs are only at the beginning of words

questions.stem: Which word has the same vowel sound as 'boy'?
hints: 'Boy' has the /oi/ sound.
Which word also has the /oi/ sound?
questions.explanation: 'Toy' has the same /oi/ sound as 'boy'.

questions.stem: Which word has the same vowel sound as 'day'?
hints: 'Day' has the /ei/ sound.
Which word also has the /ei/ sound?
questions.explanation: 'Play' has the same /ei/ sound as 'day'.

questions.stem: What vowel sound do you hear in the word 'my'?
hints: Say 'my' slowly.
It sounds like 'eye'.
questions.explanation: The word 'my' has the /ai/ sound, like in 'why'.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses a word with the /oi/ sound?
options: The boy plays with a toy.
The cat sits on the mat.
The cup is on the table.
The pen is in the bag.
hints: The /oi/ sound is in 'boy' and 'toy'.
Which sentence has these words?
questions.explanation: 'The boy plays with a toy' uses 'boy' and 'toy', which have the /oi/ sound.

questions.stem: Which word does NOT have the /ai/ sound?
hints: 'Try', 'my' and 'why' all have the /ai/ sound.
Which word has a different vowel sound?
questions.explanation: 'Tree' has the /i/ sound, not the /ai/ sound. 'Try', 'my' and 'why' all have the /ai/ sound.

questions.stem: What vowel sound do you hear in the word 'coin'?
hints: Say 'coin' slowly.
It sounds like 'oy' in 'boy'.
questions.explanation: The word 'coin' has the /oi/ sound, like in 'boy'.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses a word with the /ai/ sound?
hints: The /ai/ sound is in 'sky' and 'my'.
Which sentence has a word with that sound?
questions.explanation: 'I can see the sky' uses 'sky', which has the /ai/ sound.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses a word with the /ei/ sound?
hints: The /ei/ sound is in 'train' and 'late'.
Which sentence has these words?
questions.explanation: 'The train is late' uses 'train' and 'late', which have the /ei/ sound.

questions.stem: Which word has the /oi/ sound?
hints: The /oi/ sound is in 'boy'.
Which word has the same sound?
questions.explanation: 'Boy' has the /oi/ sound.

questions.stem: Which word has the /ei/ sound?
hints: The /ei/ sound is in 'day' and 'play'.
Which word has the same sound?
questions.explanation: 'Name' has the /ei/ sound.

questions.stem: Which word contains the /oi/ sound?
hints: The /oi/ sound is in 'boy' and 'toy'.
Which word has the same sound?
questions.explanation: 'Coin' contains the /oi/ sound.

questions.stem: Which word has a different vowel sound from the others?
hints: Three words have the /ei/ sound.
Which word has a different vowel sound?
questions.explanation: 'Day', 'play' and 'say' have the /ei/ sound. 'Tree' has the /i/ sound.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses a word with the /ei/ sound?
hints: The /ei/ sound is in 'rainbow'.
Which sentence has a word with that sound?
questions.explanation: 'I can see a rainbow' uses 'rainbow', which has the /ei/ sound.

questions.stem: Which word does NOT have the /oi/ sound?
hints: 'Boy', 'toy' and 'coin' all have the /oi/ sound.
Which word has a different vowel sound?
questions.explanation: 'Cat' does not have the /oi/ sound; it has the /æ/ sound.

questions.stem: Which word has the same vowel sound as 'pie'?
hints: 'Pie' has the /ai/ sound.
Which word also has the /ai/ sound?
questions.explanation: 'Tie' has the same /ai/ sound as 'pie'.

questions.stem: A pupil says 'The train goes to Accra.' Which word in the sentence has the /ei/ sound?
hints: The /ei/ sound is in 'day' and 'play'.
Which word in the sentence has the same sound?
questions.explanation: 'Train' has the /ei/ sound.

indicator.subject: English Language
indicator.content_standard: B4.2.5.1: Identify and use consonant blends and clusters in reading
indicator.objective: Orally produce single-syllable words by blending sounds (phonemes), including consonant blends

skills.description: Recognise consonant blends (bl, br, cl, cr, gl, gr, etc.) in words
Read single-syllable words with consonant blends correctly
Orally blend sounds to produce words with consonant blends
Use words with consonant blends in meaningful sentences

spec.difficultyPlan: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4
misconceptions: A blend is two separate sounds
Blends are only at the beginning of words
You can add any consonant to make a blend

questions.stem: Which word begins with the blend 'bl'?
hints: The blend 'bl' has both 'b' and 'l' sounds.
Say the word slowly: b-l-ack.
questions.explanation: 'Black' begins with the blend 'bl' — you can hear both /b/ and /l/ sounds.

questions.stem: What is the blend at the beginning of 'grow'?
hints: Say 'grow' slowly: g-r-ow.
The first two sounds are /g/ and /r/.
questions.explanation: 'Grow' begins with the blend 'gr' (/g/ + /r/).

questions.stem: Which word has the blend 'cr'?
hints: The blend 'cr' has both 'c' and 'r' sounds.
Say 'crab' slowly: c-r-ab.
questions.explanation: 'Crab' has the blend 'cr' — you hear both /k/ and /r/ sounds.

questions.stem: Which word has the blend 'gl'?
hints: The blend 'gl' has both 'g' and 'l' sounds.
Say 'glass' slowly: g-l-ass.
questions.explanation: 'Glass' has the blend 'gl' — you hear both /g/ and /l/ sounds.

questions.stem: Which word begins with a different blend from the others?
hints: Three words begin with 'bl'.
One word begins with a different blend.
questions.explanation: 'Blue', 'black' and 'block' begin with 'bl'. 'Brown' begins with 'br'.

questions.stem: Read this word: 'plum'. What blend does it begin with?
hints: Say 'plum' slowly: p-l-um.
The first two sounds are /p/ and /l/.
questions.explanation: 'Plum' begins with the blend 'pl' (/p/ + /l/).

questions.stem: Which word has the blend 'tr'?
hints: The blend 'tr' has both 't' and 'r' sounds.
Say 'tree' slowly: t-r-ee.
questions.explanation: 'Tree' has the blend 'tr' — you hear both /t/ and /r/ sounds.

questions.stem: Which word can be made by blending /s/ + /t/ + /ɒ/ + /p/?
hints: Blend the sounds together: s-t-o-p.
The word has the blend 'st'.
questions.explanation: Blending /s/ + /t/ + /ɒ/ + /p/ gives 'stop'.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses a word with the blend 'gr'?
hints: The blend 'gr' is in 'grass' and 'green'.
Which sentence has these words?
questions.explanation: 'The grass is green' uses 'grass' and 'green', which have the blend 'gr'.

questions.stem: Which word has the blend 'st'?
hints: The blend 'st' has both 's' and 't' sounds.
Say 'star' slowly: s-t-ar.
questions.explanation: 'Star' has the blend 'st' — you hear both /s/ and /t/ sounds.

questions.stem: Which word has a blend at the BEGINNING and a blend at the END?
hints: Look for a word that starts with 'st' and ends with 'mp'.
Say each word slowly and listen for two blends.
questions.explanation: 'Stamp' begins with 'st' and ends with 'mp' — it has blends at both the beginning and the end.
misconceptions: Only stamp has blends at both ends; stop and step have no ending blend.

questions.stem: Which set of words all begin with the same blend?
hints: Look for the set where all three words begin with the same two letters.
'Blue', 'black' and 'block' all begin with 'bl'.
questions.explanation: 'Blue', 'black' and 'block' all begin with the blend 'bl'. The other sets mix different blends.
misconceptions: The other sets mix different beginning blends.

questions.stem: A pupil says the sounds /s/ /t/ /r/ /i/ /ŋ/. What word are they blending?
hints: Blend the sounds: s-t-r-i-ng.
The word has the blend 'str'.
questions.explanation: Blending /s/ + /t/ + /r/ + /i/ + /ŋ/ gives 'string'.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses TWO words with consonant blends?
hints: Look for a sentence with more than one word containing a blend.
'Green' has 'gr' and 'frog' has 'fr'.
questions.explanation: 'The green frog jumped' uses 'green' (blend 'gr') and 'frog' (blend 'fr').
misconceptions: 'The cup is red' has no blends.

questions.stem: Which word does NOT begin with a consonant blend?
hints: A consonant blend has two consonant sounds together.
'Ship' begins with 'sh' — a digraph (one sound), not a blend.
questions.explanation: 'Ship' begins with 'sh', which is a digraph (one sound), not a blend. 'Stop', 'clap' and 'bring' all begin with blends.

indicator.subject: English Language
indicator.content_standard: B4.2.6.1: Understand word meanings and usages
indicator.objective: Use level-appropriate content words (nouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs) and function words (prepositions) appropriately in spoken and written communication

skills.description: Identify and use content words (nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs) in sentences
Identify and use function words (prepositions) in sentences
Sort words into content words and function words
Construct meaningful sentences using both content and function words

spec.difficultyPlan: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4
misconceptions: Any word can be a content word

questions.stem: Which word is a noun?
hints: A noun names a person, place, thing or animal.
A table is a thing.
questions.explanation: 'Table' is a noun because it names an object.

questions.stem: Which word is a verb?
hints: A verb is an action word.
Jumping is an action.
questions.explanation: 'Jump' is a verb because it is an action word.

questions.stem: Which word is a preposition?
hints: A preposition shows position or relationship.
'Under' shows position.
questions.explanation: 'Under' is a preposition because it shows position.

questions.stem: Which word is an adjective?
hints: An adjective describes a noun.
'Beautiful' describes something.
questions.explanation: 'Beautiful' is an adjective because it describes a noun.

questions.stem: Which word is a content word?
hints: Content words carry specific meaning (nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs).
'Mango' is a noun with specific meaning.
questions.explanation: 'Mango' is a content word because it is a noun with specific meaning. 'Under', 'at' and 'the' are function words.

questions.stem: Which word in the sentence 'The tall boy runs quickly' is a verb?
hints: The verb is the action word.
What is the boy doing?
questions.explanation: 'Runs' is the verb because it shows the action.

questions.stem: Which word in the sentence 'The book is on the table' is a preposition?
hints: A preposition shows position.
'On' shows where the book is.
questions.explanation: 'On' is the preposition because it shows position.

questions.stem: Which of these is a function word?
hints: Function words show grammatical relationships.
'In' is a preposition, a function word.
questions.explanation: 'In' is a function word because it is a preposition showing relationship.

questions.stem: Which word in the sentence 'She sings beautifully' is an adverb?
hints: An adverb describes how the action is done.
How does she sing?
questions.explanation: 'Beautifully' is an adverb because it describes how she sings.
misconceptions: There is an adverb in the sentence.

questions.stem: Which word in the sentence 'The hungry children ate the food' is an adjective?
hints: An adjective describes a noun.
What describes the children?
questions.explanation: 'Hungry' is an adjective because it describes the children.

questions.stem: Which list contains ONLY content words?
hints: Content words are nouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs.
Which list has no prepositions or articles?
questions.explanation: 'Cat' (noun), 'run' (verb), 'happy' (adjective), 'quickly' (adverb) are all content words.

questions.stem: Which sentence contains both content words and function words?
options: The cat sat on the mat.
hints: A complete sentence needs both content words (nouns, verbs) and function words (prepositions, articles).
Which sentence is complete?
questions.explanation: 'The cat sat on the mat' contains content words (cat, sat, mat) and function words (the, on, the).

questions.stem: Which sentence uses a content word and a function word correctly?
hints: A correct sentence needs a subject, verb and complete thought.
Which sentence is complete and meaningful?
questions.explanation: 'The boy runs to school' uses content words (boy, runs, school) and function words (the, to) correctly.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'She quickly ate the delicious mango', which word is an adverb?
hints: An adverb describes how the action is done.
How did she eat?
questions.explanation: 'Quickly' is the adverb because it describes how she ate.

questions.stem: Which sentence contains THREE content words and TWO function words?
options: The cat sat on the mat.
hints: Count the content words (nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs) and function words (prepositions, articles, auxiliaries).
'The boy runs to school' has content: boy, runs, school; function: the, to.
questions.explanation: 'The boy runs to school' has 3 content words (boy, runs, school) and 2 function words (the, to).
misconceptions: 'The cat sat on the mat' has 3 content words and 3 function words.
'She sings' has 2 content words and 0 function words.
'They are playing' has 2 content words and 1 function word.

indicator.subject: English Language
indicator.content_standard: B4.2.6.1: Understand word meanings and usages
indicator.objective: Use the following terms: compound word, idiom, simile, synonym, antonym, pre-fix, suffix, phrasal verb etc. in spoken and written expressions

skills.description: Recognise and define key vocabulary terms (compound word, idiom, simile, synonym, antonym, prefix, suffix, phrasal verb)
Give examples of each term
Use words related to these terms in sentences

spec.difficultyPlan: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4
misconceptions: Synonyms are words that sound the same
Antonyms are words that are spelled the same
A prefix and a suffix are the same
Idioms mean exactly what the words say

questions.stem: What is a synonym?
options: A word with the same or similar meaning
A word with the opposite meaning
A word made of two words
A word that sounds the same
hints: Synonyms have similar meanings.
'Happy' and 'glad' are synonyms.
questions.explanation: A synonym is a word that has the same or a similar meaning to another word.
misconceptions: Two words combined is a compound word.
Sounding the same is a homophone.

questions.stem: What is an antonym?
options: A word with the opposite meaning
A word with the same meaning
A word made of two words
hints: Antonyms have opposite meanings.
'Hot' and 'cold' are antonyms.
questions.explanation: An antonym is a word that has the opposite meaning to another word.
misconceptions: Two words combined is a compound word.
A prefix is part of a word, not an antonym.

questions.stem: What is a compound word?
options: A word made by joining two or more words
A word that means the opposite
hints: Compound words are formed by combining words.
'Sunflower' is made of 'sun' + 'flower'.
questions.explanation: A compound word is made by joining two or more words together, e.g. 'sunflower' = sun + flower.
misconceptions: A prefix is added to a root word.
A suffix is added to the end of a word.

questions.stem: What is a prefix?
options: A letter or group of letters added to the beginning of a word
A letter or group of letters added to the end of a word
A word made of two words
A word that sounds the same
hints: A prefix comes at the beginning.
'Un-' in 'unhappy' is a prefix.
questions.explanation: A prefix is a letter or group of letters added to the beginning of a word to change its meaning.
misconceptions: A suffix is added to the end.
A compound word is two words joined.
Sounding the same is a homophone.

questions.stem: What is a suffix?
options: A letter or group of letters added to the end of a word
A letter or group of letters added to the beginning of a word
A word made of two words
A word that means the opposite
hints: A suffix comes at the end.
'-ness' in 'kindness' is a suffix.
questions.explanation: A suffix is a letter or group of letters added to the end of a word to change its meaning or form.
misconceptions: A prefix is added to the beginning.
A compound word is two words joined.

questions.stem: Which of these is a compound word?
hints: A compound word is made of two or more words.
'Sunflower' = sun + flower.
questions.explanation: 'Sunflower' is a compound word made from 'sun' and 'flower'.

questions.stem: Which word is a synonym of 'happy'?
hints: A synonym has a similar meaning.
'Glad' means the same as 'happy'.
questions.explanation: 'Glad' is a synonym of 'happy' because they have similar meanings.

questions.stem: Which word is an antonym of 'hot'?
hints: An antonym has the opposite meaning.
'Hot' and 'cold' are opposites.
questions.explanation: 'Cold' is an antonym of 'hot' because they have opposite meanings.

questions.stem: Which word has the prefix 'un-'?
hints: The prefix 'un-' is at the beginning.
'Unhappy' = un + happy.
questions.explanation: 'Unhappy' has the prefix 'un-' added to the root word 'happy'.

questions.stem: Which word has the suffix '-ness'?
hints: The suffix '-ness' is at the end.
'Kindness' = kind + ness.
questions.explanation: 'Kindness' has the suffix '-ness' added to the root word 'kind'.

questions.stem: What is a simile?
options: A word with the opposite meaning
A word made of two words
hints: Similes compare two things.
They use 'like' or 'as'.
questions.explanation: A simile is a comparison using 'like' or 'as', e.g. 'as brave as a lion'.
misconceptions: Two words combined is a compound word.
A prefix is part of a word.

questions.stem: Which sentence contains a simile?
options: She is as brave as a lion.
hints: A simile uses 'like' or 'as' to compare.
'As brave as a lion' is a simile.
questions.explanation: 'She is as brave as a lion' is a simile because it compares her bravery to a lion using 'as'.
misconceptions: 'She is brave' is a plain statement.
'She is not brave' is a negative statement.
'She has bravery' is not a simile.

questions.stem: What is an idiom?
options: A phrase with a meaning different from the literal meaning of its words
A word made of two words
hints: Idioms have figurative meanings.
'To pull someone's leg' means to joke with them.
questions.explanation: An idiom is a phrase whose meaning is different from the literal meaning of its individual words.
misconceptions: Two words combined is a compound word.
A prefix is part of a word.
A simile is a comparison using 'like' or 'as'.

questions.stem: Which of these is an idiom?
hints: An idiom has a figurative meaning.
'To pull someone's leg' means to joke with someone, not to literally pull their leg.
questions.explanation: 'To pull someone's leg' is an idiom meaning to joke with someone.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the synonym of 'quick' correctly?
hints: A synonym of 'quick' is 'fast'.
Which sentence uses 'fast'?
questions.explanation: 'The fast car zoomed by' uses 'fast', which is a synonym of 'quick'.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the prefix 're-' correctly?
options: She had to rewrite the letter.
hints: 'Re-' means 'again'.
'Rewrite' means to write again.
questions.explanation: 'She had to rewrite the letter' uses 'rewrite' with the prefix 're-' meaning 'again'.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses an idiom correctly?
options: She was feeling under the weather, so she stayed home.
She was under the weather literally.
She put the weather under something.
hints: 'Under the weather' is an idiom meaning 'feeling sick'.
Which sentence uses the idiom figuratively?
questions.explanation: 'She was feeling under the weather, so she stayed home' uses the idiom correctly — it means she was feeling sick.
misconceptions: The other options use the phrase literally or incorrectly.

indicator.subject: English Language
indicator.content_standard: B4.2.6.2: Build vocabulary
indicator.objective: Develop a rich vocabulary stock through extensive reading of age-appropriate texts

skills.description: Identify the meaning of new words from context
Use new vocabulary in sentences
Recognise the purpose of a vocabulary portfolio (collecting and using new words)

spec.difficultyPlan: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4
misconceptions: You only learn vocabulary from a dictionary
A word has only one meaning
You don't need to use new words

questions.stem: Read this sentence: 'The plant began to wither because it had no water.' What does 'wither' mean?
hints: The plant had no water.
What happens to a plant without water?
questions.explanation: 'Wither' means to dry up and die, especially because of lack of water.
misconceptions: Producing flowers is not related to drying up.

questions.stem: Read: 'The baby was drowsy after feeding and soon fell asleep.' What does 'drowsy' mean?
hints: The baby fell asleep soon after.
What feeling makes you fall asleep?
questions.explanation: 'Drowsy' means sleepy or ready to fall asleep.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the word 'enormous' correctly?
options: The enormous ant was smaller than my finger.
The enormous elephant filled the whole path.
The enormous pencil was easy to carry.
The enormous cup was too small for tea.
hints: 'Enormous' means very large.
Which sentence describes something very large?
questions.explanation: 'The enormous elephant filled the whole path' uses 'enormous' correctly because an elephant is very large.
misconceptions: The ant is described as small.
The pencil is described as easy to carry (small).
The cup is described as too small.

questions.stem: What is a vocabulary portfolio?
options: A book where you write new words and their meanings
A book for spelling tests only
hints: A portfolio is a collection of work.
A vocabulary portfolio collects new words.
questions.explanation: A vocabulary portfolio is a book or folder where you collect new words, their meanings and example sentences.
misconceptions: Drawing pictures is not the main purpose.
Spelling tests are only part of it.

questions.stem: Read: 'The path was narrow, so only one person could pass at a time.' What does 'narrow' mean?
hints: Only one person could pass.
It means the opposite of wide.
questions.explanation: 'Narrow' means not wide — only a small width.
misconceptions: Long is about length, not width.
Short is about length, not width.

questions.stem: Read: 'The teacher commended Ama for her excellent work.' What does 'commended' mean?
hints: The teacher was happy with Ama's excellent work.
What would a teacher do for excellent work?
questions.explanation: 'Commended' means praised or spoke well of someone.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the word 'fragile' correctly?
options: The fragile glass broke when it fell.
The fragile stone was very strong.
The fragile tree was hard to bend.
hints: 'Fragile' means easily broken.
Which sentence describes something that breaks easily?
questions.explanation: 'The fragile glass broke when it fell' uses 'fragile' correctly because glass breaks easily.
misconceptions: A hard tree is not fragile.
Indestructible metal is the opposite of fragile.

questions.stem: What should you write in your vocabulary portfolio?
options: Only the spelling of new words
The new word, its meaning and an example sentence
Only a drawing of the word
Only the page number in the dictionary
hints: A good portfolio entry helps you remember the word.
Include meaning and an example.
questions.explanation: A good vocabulary portfolio entry includes the new word, its meaning and an example sentence to show how it is used.
misconceptions: A drawing alone is not enough.
Page numbers alone are not useful.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the word 'reluctant' correctly?
options: She was reluctant to eat the cake and ate it quickly.
He was reluctant to go to the party, so he stayed home.
They were reluctant to win the prize.
I was reluctant to be happy.
hints: 'Reluctant' means not wanting to do something.
Which sentence shows someone not wanting to do something?
questions.explanation: 'He was reluctant to go to the party, so he stayed home' uses 'reluctant' correctly.
misconceptions: Eating quickly shows willingness, not reluctance.
Winning a prize is positive; reluctant is negative.
Being happy is positive; reluctant is negative.

questions.stem: Read: 'The old man was very frail and needed help walking.' What does 'frail' mean?
hints: The old man needed help walking.
He is not strong.
questions.explanation: 'Frail' means weak and fragile, especially because of age or illness.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the word 'abundant' correctly?
options: The abundant water dried up completely.
The farm had an abundant harvest of maize.
The abundant food was not enough for anyone.
There was an abundant shortage of books.
hints: 'Abundant' means plenty or more than enough.
Which sentence describes a large amount?
questions.explanation: 'The farm had an abundant harvest of maize' uses 'abundant' correctly to mean a large harvest.
misconceptions: Dried up completely is the opposite of abundant.
Not enough is the opposite of abundant.
A shortage is the opposite of abundant.

questions.stem: Read: 'She was very cautious when crossing the busy road.' What does 'cautious' mean?
hints: The road was busy.
What should you be when crossing a busy road?
questions.explanation: 'Cautious' means careful to avoid danger or problems.

questions.stem: Read: 'The teacher's explanation was so clear that even the most confused pupils understood.' What does 'confused' mean?
hints: The explanation helped them understand.
They were confused before the explanation.
questions.explanation: 'Confused' means not understanding something clearly.
misconceptions: Very happy is not the meaning.
Very tired is not the meaning.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the word 'vivid' correctly?
options: The vivid colours of the kente cloth caught everyone's attention.
The vivid picture was dull and boring.
The vivid sound was very quiet.
hints: 'Vivid' means bright and intense.
Which sentence describes something bright and striking?
questions.explanation: 'The vivid colours of the kente cloth caught everyone's attention' uses 'vivid' correctly to mean bright and striking.
misconceptions: Dull and boring is the opposite of vivid.
Bland is the opposite of vivid taste.

questions.stem: How can a vocabulary portfolio help you in your reading?
options: It helps you remember new words and understand texts better
It helps you skip difficult words
It replaces the need to read
hints: A portfolio collects new words.
Knowing more words helps you understand texts.
questions.explanation: A vocabulary portfolio helps you remember new words, which helps you understand texts better when reading.
misconceptions: It does not make reading longer.
It does not help you skip words.

questions.stem: Read: 'The football match was postponed because of heavy rain.' What does 'postponed' mean?
hints: Heavy rain prevented the match from happening now.
It will happen later.
questions.explanation: 'Postponed' means moved to a later time or date.
misconceptions: Cancelled means it will not happen at all.
Played in the rain is not the meaning.

indicator.subject: English Language
indicator.content_standard: B4.2.6.3: Demonstrate a rich vocabulary that supports the development of listening, reading, speaking, writing and presentation skills
indicator.objective: Deduce meaning of words from how they are used in context e.g. near synonyms: cool – cold – freezing), homonyms: flour/flower

skills.description: Use surrounding words to deduce the meaning of an unfamiliar word
Distinguish between near synonyms (cool/cold/freezing) based on context
Recognise homonyms (words that sound the same but have different meanings/spellings)

spec.difficultyPlan: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4
misconceptions: You can guess any word's meaning without context
Homonyms are always spelled the same
Context clues are always in the same sentence

questions.stem: Read: 'The soup was so hot that it burnt my tongue.' What does 'hot' mean in this sentence?
hints: The soup burnt the tongue.
That tells you it was at a high temperature.
questions.explanation: In this context, 'hot' means high temperature because it burnt the tongue.
misconceptions: Spicy food does not necessarily burn the tongue in this way.
Popular is a different meaning of 'hot'.
Stolen is a different meaning of 'hot'.

questions.stem: Read: 'The baby was crying because she was famished.' What does 'famished' mean?
hints: The baby was crying.
Crying babies often need food.
questions.explanation: 'Famished' means very hungry, which is why the baby was crying.
misconceptions: Sleepy is not indicated by crying for food.
Happy babies usually do not cry.
Angry is possible, but 'famished' means hungry.

questions.stem: Which word best describes weather that is slightly cold but comfortable?
hints: 'Freezing' is very cold.
'Cool' is slightly cold and comfortable.
questions.explanation: 'Cool' best describes weather that is slightly cold but comfortable.

questions.stem: Which pair are homonyms?
hints: Homonyms sound the same but have different meanings.
'Flour' and 'flower' sound the same but mean different things.
questions.explanation: 'Flour' and 'flower' are homonyms — they sound the same but have different meanings and spellings.

questions.stem: Read: 'The old bridge was dilapidated; parts of it had fallen into the river.' What does 'dilapidated' mean?
hints: Parts of the bridge had fallen into the river.
This shows it is old and broken.
questions.explanation: 'Dilapidated' means falling apart or in a state of disrepair.
misconceptions: New and strong is the opposite.
Long is about length, not condition.

questions.stem: Read: 'The pupil was scolded for being tardy to class three times in one week.' What does 'tardy' mean?
hints: The pupil was scolded.
Coming late to class is a reason to be scolded.
questions.explanation: 'Tardy' means late, which is why the pupil was scolded.
misconceptions: Absent means not there at all.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'The water was freezing, so we could not swim', which word could replace 'freezing' without changing the meaning much?
hints: 'Freezing' means extremely cold.
Which word also means very cold?
questions.explanation: 'Icy' is a near synonym of 'freezing' — both mean very cold.

questions.stem: Read: 'I can hear the sea.' Which word is a homonym with 'sea'?
hints: 'Sea' and 'see' sound the same.
They have different meanings and spellings.
questions.explanation: 'See' is a homonym of 'sea' — they sound the same but have different meanings.

questions.stem: Read: 'The farmer used a hoe to till the soil before planting.' What does 'till' mean here?
hints: The farmer used a hoe.
The purpose is to prepare the soil for planting.
questions.explanation: In this context, 'till' means to prepare the soil for planting.
misconceptions: A cash register is not related to farming.
Plow is similar but 'till' is the specific action here.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses 'right' correctly as a homonym meaning 'correct'?
options: The right to vote is important.
She has a right to know.
hints: 'Right' can mean correct, direction, or entitlement.
Which sentence uses it to mean 'correct'?
questions.explanation: 'You gave the right answer' uses 'right' to mean correct.

questions.stem: Read: 'The lecture was so tedious that many students fell asleep.' What does 'tedious' mean?
hints: Students fell asleep.
What kind of lecture makes people sleep?
questions.explanation: 'Tedious' means boring and tiresome, which is why students fell asleep.

questions.stem: Which word is a near synonym of 'happy' but suggests a quieter, more peaceful feeling?
hints: A quieter, peaceful feeling is calmer.
'Content' means quietly happy.
questions.explanation: 'Content' is a near synonym of 'happy' that suggests a quiet, peaceful feeling.

questions.stem: Which pair are homonyms?
hints: Homonyms sound the same.
'Blue' and 'blew' sound the same but have different meanings.
questions.explanation: 'Blue' (a colour) and 'blew' (past tense of blow) are homonyms.

questions.stem: Read: 'The politician's speech was ambiguous, so nobody knew exactly what he meant.' What does 'ambiguous' mean?
options: Unclear or having more than one meaning
hints: Nobody knew exactly what he meant.
The speech was unclear.
questions.explanation: 'Ambiguous' means unclear or having more than one possible meaning.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'The house was small but cosy', which word could replace 'cosy' without changing the feeling much?
hints: 'Cosy' means warm and comfortable.
Which word has a similar positive feeling?
questions.explanation: 'Comfortable' is a near synonym of 'cosy' — both suggest a warm, pleasant feeling.

questions.stem: Read: 'The generous woman donated food to the orphanage every month.' What does 'generous' mean?
hints: She donated food every month.
This shows she likes to give.
questions.explanation: 'Generous' means willing to give freely to others.
misconceptions: Being rich is not the meaning.
Being poor is not the meaning.

questions.stem: Read: 'The wind blew the leaves off the tree.' Which word is a homonym of 'blew'?
hints: 'Blew' sounds like a colour.
The homonym is 'blue'.
questions.explanation: 'Blue' is a homonym of 'blew' — they sound the same but have different meanings and spellings.
misconceptions: 'Blow' is the present tense, not a homonym.

questions.stem: Which set of words is arranged from least intense to most intense?
hints: Least intense means mildest.
Warm is mild, hot is stronger, boiling is strongest.
questions.explanation: 'Warm, hot, boiling' is arranged from least intense to most intense.
misconceptions: The other options are not in order of intensity.

questions.stem: Read: 'The teacher's explanation was concise but complete; she covered all the points in just five minutes.' What does 'concise' mean?
hints: She covered all the points in just five minutes.
This shows it was short but complete.
questions.explanation: 'Concise' means short and clear, giving the necessary information without extra words.
misconceptions: Long and detailed is the opposite.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses 'bat' as a homonym meaning 'a piece of sports equipment'?
options: The bat flew out of the cave.
He hit the ball with a bat.
The bat is a nocturnal animal.
hints: 'Bat' can mean an animal or sports equipment.
Which sentence is about sports?
questions.explanation: 'He hit the ball with a bat' uses 'bat' to mean a piece of sports equipment.
misconceptions: 'The bat flew' is about an animal.

indicator.subject: English Language
indicator.content_standard: B4.2.6.3: Demonstrate a rich vocabulary that supports the development of listening, reading, speaking, writing and presentation skills
indicator.objective: Deduce meaning of words from how they relate to one another (synonyms, antonyms)

skills.description: Identify synonyms (words with similar meanings)
Identify antonyms (words with opposite meanings)
Use synonyms and antonyms in sentences

spec.difficultyPlan: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4
misconceptions: Synonyms have exactly the same meaning
Synonyms can always replace each other

questions.stem: Which word is a synonym of 'big'?
hints: A synonym has a similar meaning.
'Large' means the same as 'big'.
questions.explanation: 'Large' is a synonym of 'big' because they have similar meanings.
misconceptions: 'Short' is not a synonym of big.

questions.stem: Which word is an antonym of 'happy'?
hints: An antonym has the opposite meaning.
'Sad' is the opposite of 'happy'.
questions.explanation: 'Sad' is an antonym of 'happy' because they have opposite meanings.

questions.stem: Which word is a synonym of 'quick'?
hints: A synonym has a similar meaning.
'Fast' means the same as 'quick'.
questions.explanation: 'Fast' is a synonym of 'quick'.

questions.stem: Which word is an antonym of 'hot'?
hints: An antonym has the opposite meaning.
'Cold' is the opposite of 'hot'.
questions.explanation: 'Cold' is an antonym of 'hot'.

questions.stem: Which word is a synonym of 'begin'?
hints: A synonym has a similar meaning.
'Start' means the same as 'begin'.
questions.explanation: 'Start' is a synonym of 'begin'.

questions.stem: Which word is an antonym of 'difficult'?
hints: An antonym has the opposite meaning.
'Easy' is the opposite of 'difficult'.
questions.explanation: 'Easy' is an antonym of 'difficult'.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses a synonym of 'beautiful' correctly?
options: The garden was full of beautiful flowers.
The garden was full of ugly flowers.
The garden was full of small flowers.
The garden was full of dead flowers.
hints: A synonym of 'beautiful' is 'lovely' or 'pretty'.
Which sentence uses a word with a similar positive meaning?
questions.explanation: 'The garden was full of beautiful flowers' uses 'beautiful' correctly. The others use different words.

questions.stem: Which pair of words are synonyms?
hints: Synonyms have similar meanings.
'Happy' and 'joyful' mean almost the same thing.
questions.explanation: 'Happy' and 'joyful' are synonyms because they have similar meanings.

questions.stem: Which pair of words are antonyms?
hints: Antonyms have opposite meanings.
'Love' and 'hate' are opposites.
questions.explanation: 'Love' and 'hate' are antonyms because they have opposite meanings.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses an antonym of 'strong' correctly?
options: The weak boy could not lift the box.
The strong boy lifted the box.
The tall boy lifted the box.
The happy boy lifted the box.
hints: An antonym of 'strong' is 'weak'.
Which sentence uses 'weak'?
questions.explanation: 'The weak boy could not lift the box' uses 'weak', an antonym of 'strong', correctly.

questions.stem: Which word is the best synonym for 'brave' in the sentence 'The brave soldier fought in the war'?
hints: A synonym has a similar meaning.
'Courageous' means the same as 'brave'.
questions.explanation: 'Courageous' is the best synonym for 'brave' because it has the same meaning.

questions.stem: Which word is the best antonym for 'generous' in the sentence 'The generous man shared his food'?
hints: An antonym has the opposite meaning.
'Selfish' is the opposite of 'generous'.
questions.explanation: 'Selfish' is the best antonym for 'generous' because it has the opposite meaning.

questions.stem: Read: 'The teacher was very pleased with the pupils' work.' Which word is a synonym of 'pleased'?
hints: A synonym has a similar meaning.
'Happy' means the same as 'pleased'.
questions.explanation: 'Happy' is a synonym of 'pleased'.

questions.stem: Which word is a synonym of 'ancient'?
hints: A synonym has a similar meaning.
'Old' means the same as 'ancient'.
questions.explanation: 'Old' is a synonym of 'ancient'.

indicator.subject: English Language
indicator.content_standard: B4.2.6.4: Use words appropriately for purpose, audience, context and culture
indicator.objective: Expand vocabulary stock through affixation

skills.description: Recognise prefixes and suffixes in words
Understand how affixes change word meaning
Form new words by adding prefixes and suffixes to root words

spec.difficultyPlan: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4
misconceptions: Affixes are the main part of a word
Adding an affix always changes the word class
Suffixes and prefixes are the same

questions.stem: What is the prefix in the word 'unhappy'?
hints: A prefix is added at the beginning of a word.
In 'unhappy', 'un-' comes before 'happy'.
questions.explanation: The prefix in 'unhappy' is 'un-', which is added to the root word 'happy'.

questions.stem: What is the suffix in the word 'kindness'?
hints: A suffix is added at the end of a word.
In 'kindness', '-ness' comes after 'kind'.
questions.explanation: The suffix in 'kindness' is '-ness', which is added to the root word 'kind'.

questions.stem: What does the prefix 'un-' usually mean?
hints: Think of 'unhappy' — what does it mean?
'Un-' makes a word mean the opposite.
questions.explanation: The prefix 'un-' usually means 'not' or 'the opposite of' (e.g. unhappy = not happy).

questions.stem: What does the suffix '-less' mean in the word 'careless'?
hints: 'Careless' means without care.
'-less' means 'without'.
questions.explanation: The suffix '-less' means 'without', so 'careless' means without care.

questions.stem: Which word has a suffix?
hints: A suffix comes at the end.
'-ly' is a common suffix.
questions.explanation: 'Quickly' has the suffix '-ly' added to the root word 'quick'.
misconceptions: 'Quicken' has a suffix '-en', but 'quickly' is the clear example.

questions.stem: What does the prefix 're-' mean in 'rewrite'?
hints: 'Rewrite' means to write again.
'Re-' means 'again'.
questions.explanation: The prefix 're-' means 'again', so 'rewrite' means to write again.

questions.stem: What does the suffix '-ful' mean in 'careful'?
hints: 'Careful' means full of care.
'-ful' means 'full of'.
questions.explanation: The suffix '-ful' means 'full of', so 'careful' means full of care.

questions.stem: Add a prefix to 'happy' to make a word meaning 'not happy'.
hints: The prefix 'un-' means 'not'.
So 'unhappy' means not happy.
questions.explanation: Adding the prefix 'un-' to 'happy' gives 'unhappy', meaning not happy.
misconceptions: 'Dis-' can mean not, but 'dishappy' is not standard.

questions.stem: Add a suffix to 'care' to make a word meaning 'without care'.
hints: The suffix '-less' means 'without'.
So 'careless' means without care.
questions.explanation: Adding the suffix '-less' to 'care' gives 'careless', meaning without care.

questions.stem: What does the word 'preview' mean?
hints: The prefix 'pre-' means 'before'.
So 'preview' means to view before.
questions.explanation: 'Preview' means to view something before it is shown to others.

questions.stem: Which word has both a prefix and a suffix?
hints: Look for a word with something added at the beginning and at the end.
'Unhappiness' = un- + happy + -ness.
questions.explanation: 'Unhappiness' has both a prefix ('un-') and a suffix ('-ness').

questions.stem: Which word is formed by adding the prefix 'dis-' to 'agree'?
hints: The prefix 'dis-' means 'not' or 'opposite'.
So 'disagree' means not agree.
questions.explanation: Adding 'dis-' to 'agree' gives 'disagree', meaning not agree.

questions.stem: What does the word 'misunderstand' mean?
hints: The prefix 'mis-' means 'wrongly'.
So 'misunderstand' means to understand wrongly.
questions.explanation: 'Misunderstand' means to understand wrongly or incorrectly.

questions.stem: What does the suffix '-er' mean in the word 'teacher'?
hints: A teacher is a person who teaches.
'-er' often means 'a person who does something'.
questions.explanation: The suffix '-er' in 'teacher' means 'a person who teaches'.

questions.stem: Which word contains a prefix meaning 'before'?
hints: 'Pre-' means 'before'.
'Prehistoric' means before written history.
questions.explanation: 'Prehistoric' contains the prefix 'pre-' meaning 'before'.

indicator.subject: English Language
indicator.content_standard: B4.2.6.4: Use words appropriately for purpose, audience, context and culture
indicator.objective: Recognize the playful use of words in spoken and written language (jokes, riddles)

skills.description: Understand and solve simple riddles
Recognise the playful use of words in jokes (puns, wordplay)
Create or complete a simple riddle or joke

spec.difficultyPlan: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4
misconceptions: Any answer to a riddle is correct

questions.stem: Riddle: 'I have hands but cannot clap. What am I?'
hints: Think about things with hands that don't clap.
A clock has hands but cannot clap.
questions.explanation: A clock has hands (the pointers) but cannot clap.
misconceptions: A dog has paws, not hands.
A tree has branches, not hands.

questions.stem: Riddle: 'I am something that came into this world with earrings. What am I?'
hints: A coal pot has handles on the sides that look like earrings.
It is used for cooking.
questions.explanation: A coal pot has loops on its sides that look like earrings when it is made.
misconceptions: A girl is born with earrings only if pierced.
A book does not have earrings.
A car does not have earrings.

questions.stem: Joke: 'Why did the boy throw the clock out of the window? He wanted to see time fly.' What makes this joke funny?
options: The word 'fly' is used in two ways
hints: 'Time flies' is a common expression meaning time goes fast.
The joke uses 'fly' literally and figuratively.
questions.explanation: The joke is funny because 'time flies' normally means time goes quickly, but here it is used literally — the clock flying out of the window.
misconceptions: Throwing things is not the source of humour.
The boy is not the source of the joke.

questions.stem: Riddle: 'What has a face but no eyes, and hands but no arms?'
hints: It has a face and hands but they are not real.
It tells time.
questions.explanation: A clock has a face and hands, but no eyes or arms.
misconceptions: A person has eyes and arms.

questions.stem: Joke: 'Why did the man put his money in the freezer? He wanted cold cash.' What makes this joke funny?
options: 'Cold cash' sounds like a real phrase but is used literally
hints: 'Cold cash' is a phrase meaning money that is readily available.
The joke uses it literally.
questions.explanation: The joke plays on the phrase 'cold cash' by putting money in the freezer to make it literally cold.
misconceptions: The man being rich is not the source of humour.

questions.stem: Riddle: 'I am full of holes but still hold water. What am I?'
hints: A sponge has many holes but can absorb water.
It is used for cleaning.
questions.explanation: A sponge is full of holes but can still hold water.
misconceptions: A bucket does not have holes.
A cup does not have holes.
A bowl does not have holes.

questions.stem: Joke: 'Why was the maths book sad? It had too many problems.' What makes this joke funny?
options: 'Problems' means both maths exercises and difficulties
hints: 'Problems' can mean maths questions or personal difficulties.
The joke uses both meanings.
questions.explanation: The joke is funny because 'problems' means both maths exercises and real-life difficulties.

questions.stem: Riddle: 'What gets wetter the more it dries?'
hints: Think about what you use to dry yourself after a bath.
It gets wet as it dries you.
questions.explanation: A towel gets wetter as it dries you.
misconceptions: A sponge can hold water but is not used for drying in this way.
A cloth could be similar but a towel is the standard answer.
A mop is for cleaning floors.

questions.stem: Complete the riddle: 'I have a tail and a head, but no body. What am I?'
hints: A coin has a head and a tail.
It has no body.
questions.explanation: A coin has a head and a tail but no body.

questions.stem: Joke: 'Why did the student eat his homework? The teacher said it was a piece of cake.' What makes this joke funny?
options: 'A piece of cake' means something easy, but the student thought it was real cake
hints: 'A piece of cake' is an idiom meaning something easy.
The student took it literally.
questions.explanation: The joke plays on the idiom 'a piece of cake' meaning easy work, but the student literally ate it.
misconceptions: The student's hunger is not the source of humour.

questions.stem: Which of these is a riddle?
options: What has an eye but cannot see? A needle.
hints: A riddle asks a puzzling question.
It has a clever answer.
questions.explanation: 'What has an eye but cannot see? A needle' is a riddle.
misconceptions: The other options are statements, not riddles.

questions.stem: Joke: 'Why did the boy bring a ladder to school? He wanted to go to high school.' What makes this joke funny?
options: 'High school' means a school for older pupils, but here it means a school that is high up
hints: 'High school' is a real type of school.
The joke uses 'high' literally.
questions.explanation: The joke plays on 'high school' by using 'high' literally — a school that is high up, which is why the boy brought a ladder.
misconceptions: The boy's climbing is not the source of humour.
School being boring is not the joke.

questions.stem: Riddle: 'The more you take, the more you leave behind. What am I?'
hints: Think about walking.
As you take steps, you leave footprints behind.
questions.explanation: Footsteps — the more steps you take, the more footprints you leave behind.
misconceptions: Money is not left behind when taken.
Food is not left behind in this way.
Water is not left behind in this way.

questions.stem: Joke: 'Why did the teacher wear sunglasses to class? Because her pupils were so bright.' What makes this joke funny?
options: 'Pupils' means both students and parts of the eye
hints: 'Pupils' can mean students or the dark centre of the eye.
Bright light affects the pupils of the eye.
questions.explanation: The joke plays on 'pupils' meaning both students and the parts of the eye that respond to bright light.
misconceptions: Teachers do not always wear sunglasses.
The pupils being noisy is not the joke.

questions.stem: Complete the joke: 'Why was the broom late for school? It ___.
hints: The joke uses wordplay with 'swept'.
'Overslept' sounds like 'overswept'.
questions.explanation: The joke is 'It overswept' — a play on 'overslept' and 'swept'.
misconceptions: The other options do not use wordplay.

questions.stem: Riddle: 'I speak without a mouth and hear without ears. I have no body, but I come alive with wind. What am I?'
hints: It repeats sound without a mouth or ears.
It is heard in mountains or empty rooms.
questions.explanation: An echo speaks (repeats sound) without a mouth and is heard without ears. It has no body but can be heard when wind carries sound.
misconceptions: A ghost is not the standard riddle answer.

questions.stem: Joke: 'Why did the farmer name his pig Ink? Because it kept running out of the pen.' What makes this joke funny?
options: 'Pen' means both a pig's enclosure and a writing instrument
hints: 'Pen' can be a pig's home or a writing tool.
Ink running out of a pen is a common phrase.
questions.explanation: The joke plays on 'pen' meaning both the pig's enclosure and a writing pen. The ink (pig) runs out of the pen (enclosure), like ink running out of a pen.
misconceptions: Pigs being funny is not the joke.
Ink being expensive is not the joke.
Farmers liking pens is not the joke.

indicator.subject: English Language
indicator.content_standard: B4.2.6.4: Use words appropriately for purpose, audience, context and culture
indicator.objective: Use words suitable for purpose, audience, context and culture in relation to type of texts (exposition/explanation)

skills.description: Identify the purpose and audience of a text (exposition/explanation)
Choose words suitable for a given purpose, audience and context
Recognise formal and informal registers and when each is appropriate

spec.difficultyPlan: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4
misconceptions: Any word works for any audience
Exposition and explanation are the same

questions.stem: A text that explains how something works is called ___.
hints: The text explains a process.
It tells you how something works.
questions.explanation: A text that explains how something works is called an explanation.
misconceptions: A letter is a message to someone.

questions.stem: A text that gives information about a topic is called ___.
hints: The text presents facts and information.
It explains or informs about a topic.
questions.explanation: A text that gives information about a topic is called an exposition.

questions.stem: You are writing an explanation about how malaria is spread. Which word is most suitable?
hints: The text is about malaria.
Malaria is spread by mosquitoes.
questions.explanation: 'Mosquito' is the correct word for an explanation about malaria.
misconceptions: 'Doggie' is informal and not about malaria.

questions.stem: Which sentence is more suitable for an explanation text?
options: Water is heated and turns into steam.
Water gets hot and goes up.
hints: An explanation uses clear, factual language.
Which sentence sounds like an explanation?
questions.explanation: 'Water is heated and turns into steam' is suitable because it uses factual, precise language.
misconceptions: 'Gets hot and goes up' is informal.
'Goes whoosh' is informal and not factual.

questions.stem: You are writing an exposition about the importance of trees for your class. Which word is most suitable?
hints: An exposition uses precise, factual words.
Trees give us oxygen.
questions.explanation: 'Oxygen' is the precise word for an exposition about trees.

questions.stem: You are writing an explanation for young children about how plants grow. Which word is most suitable?
hints: Young children need simple words.
Which word is simplest?
questions.explanation: 'Seeds' is the simplest word suitable for young children. The other words are too advanced.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses an informal register?
options: The experiment produced a clear result.
hints: Informal language is casual.
'Awesome' is an informal word.
questions.explanation: 'The experiment was totally awesome!' uses informal language ('totally awesome').

questions.stem: An explanation text about 'How to Wash Your Hands' is most likely written for ___.
hints: Who needs to learn how to wash their hands?
The text is about hygiene.
questions.explanation: An explanation about handwashing is most likely for young children learning hygiene.
misconceptions: Car mechanics are not the audience.

questions.stem: You are writing an exposition about 'The Importance of Exercise' for your classmates. Which word is most suitable?
hints: An exposition uses precise words.
Exercise is good for your health.
questions.explanation: 'Health' is the precise word for an exposition about exercise.

questions.stem: Which register is most appropriate for a letter to the headteacher?
hints: A headteacher is an official person.
Use polite, formal language.
questions.explanation: A formal register is most appropriate for a letter to the headteacher.
misconceptions: Casual is not appropriate for official letters.

questions.stem: You are writing an explanation about 'How a Bill Becomes a Law' for a class of Basic 4 pupils. Which word should you avoid?
hints: Basic 4 pupils need simple words.
'Bicameral' is too advanced.
questions.explanation: 'Bicameral' is too advanced for Basic 4 pupils. 'Law', 'parliament' and 'bill' are simpler.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the most appropriate register for an exposition text?
options: Trees are essential because they produce oxygen.
Trees are super cool and stuff.
Trees are like, really important, you know?
hints: Exposition texts use formal, factual language.
Which sentence is factual and clear?
questions.explanation: 'Trees are essential because they produce oxygen' uses appropriate formal, factual language.
misconceptions: 'Like, really important, you know?' is informal.

questions.stem: A text explains 'How to Plant a Tree' in simple steps. What is the purpose of this text?
hints: The text gives steps for planting a tree.
It explains how to do something.
questions.explanation: The purpose is to explain a process — how to plant a tree.

questions.stem: Which register is most appropriate for a text explaining 'How to Make Kpoikpoi' for a community gathering?
hints: The text is for a community gathering.
It should be clear and respectful.
questions.explanation: A semi-formal and clear register is most appropriate — it is clear and respectful for the community.
misconceptions: Very formal scientific is too advanced.
Casual and joking is not suitable for an explanation.

questions.stem: An exposition about 'The Importance of Education' is written for parents. Which word is most suitable?
hints: Parents understand words like 'opportunities'.
Education provides opportunities.
questions.explanation: 'Opportunities' is a suitable word for an exposition about education for parents.

indicator.subject: English Language
indicator.content_standard: B4.2.7.1: Process and comprehend level-appropriate texts
indicator.objective: Construct meaning from texts read

skills.description: Construct overall meaning from a short text (understand what the text is mostly about)
Use contextual clues and prior knowledge to make meaning from a text
Answer Before Reading and After Reading questions to show understanding

spec.difficultyPlan: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4
misconceptions: Reading the words is the same as understanding them
You only need to read once to understand
The main idea is always the first sentence

questions.stem: Read: 'Ama wakes up at 6 o'clock every morning. She brushes her teeth, takes her bath and eats breakfast. Then she walks to school with her sister.' What is this text mostly about?
hints: The text describes what Ama does every morning.
It tells the steps she follows before school.
questions.explanation: The text is mostly about Ama's morning routine — the things she does every morning before school.
misconceptions: Family is only mentioned briefly (her sister).
Food is only mentioned as breakfast.

questions.stem: Read: 'Kojo has a small farm. He grows maize and cassava. He also has three goats and some chickens.' How many goats does Kojo have?
hints: Look for the number of goats in the text.
The text says 'three goats'.
questions.explanation: The text says Kojo has three goats.

questions.stem: Read: 'The sky was dark and the wind was blowing strongly. People hurried home.' What were people likely expecting?
hints: The sky was dark and the wind was blowing.
This usually means bad weather is coming.
questions.explanation: People were likely expecting rain or a storm because the sky was dark and the wind was strong.
misconceptions: Sunshine does not match a dark sky.
A football match is not indicated.

questions.stem: Read: 'The teacher asked the pupils to keep the classroom clean. They swept the floor, arranged the desks and threw rubbish into the bin.' What is this text about?
hints: The text describes sweeping, arranging desks and throwing rubbish.
All these actions are about cleanliness.
questions.explanation: The text is about keeping the classroom clean.
misconceptions: Building a classroom is not mentioned.
A school trip is not mentioned.

questions.stem: Read: 'Esi went to the market to buy tomatoes. She also bought onions and pepper.' What did Esi go to the market to buy?
hints: The text mentions three things Esi bought.
Look for the items listed.
questions.explanation: Esi went to the market to buy tomatoes, onions and pepper.
misconceptions: Fish and meat are not mentioned.

questions.stem: Read: 'Yaw found a purse on his way to school. He opened it and saw some money inside. He decided to take it to the headteacher.' What is the main idea of this text?
options: Yaw was honest when he found a purse
hints: Yaw could have kept the money but chose to hand it in.
This shows honesty.
questions.explanation: The main idea is that Yaw was honest — he chose to take the purse to the headteacher instead of keeping it.
misconceptions: The text does not say Yaw is rich.
He found a purse, not a school bag.
He found a purse, not a school.

questions.stem: Read: 'The sun was very hot. The children were sweating and looking for shade. They sat under a big tree to rest.' Why did the children sit under the tree?
options: To get shade from the hot sun
hints: The sun was very hot and they were sweating.
A tree provides shade.
questions.explanation: The children sat under the tree to get shade from the hot sun.
misconceptions: The text does not mention a game.
The text does not mention lunch.

questions.stem: Read: 'The market was crowded. Women carried baskets on their heads. Traders called out their prices. Children ran between the stalls.' What was the market like?
hints: The text says the market was crowded.
Many people were there.
questions.explanation: The market was busy and crowded — there were many people, traders and children.
misconceptions: The text does not say it was quiet.
It was not described as small and dark.

questions.stem: Read: 'Nana Yaa takes good care of her teeth. She brushes them twice a day. She visits the dentist every six months. She does not eat too many sweets.' What is the text mostly about?
options: How Nana Yaa takes care of her teeth
hints: All the sentences describe what she does for her teeth.
Brushing, visiting the dentist and avoiding sweets are all about dental care.
questions.explanation: The text is mostly about how Nana Yaa takes care of her teeth.
misconceptions: Food is only mentioned as something she avoids.

questions.stem: Read: 'The pot of soup was on the fire. After some time, a pleasant smell filled the kitchen.' What does 'pleasant' mean in this sentence?
hints: The smell filled the kitchen and was from soup cooking.
A good smell is pleasant.
questions.explanation: 'Pleasant' means nice or enjoyable — the soup smelled good.

questions.stem: Read: 'The pupils of Basic 4 went on a trip to Kakum National Park. They saw many trees and animals. They walked on the canopy walkway. Everyone enjoyed the trip.' What did the pupils see at Kakum?
hints: The text says they saw trees and animals.
Kakum is a national park with forests.
questions.explanation: The pupils saw many trees and animals at Kakum National Park.
misconceptions: A big city is not mentioned.
A river and bridge are not mentioned.

questions.stem: Read: 'Clean water is important for good health. It prevents diseases. We use it for drinking, cooking and washing. Everyone should have access to clean water.' What is the main idea?
options: Clean water is important for health
Water is used for cooking only
Dirty water is good for health
hints: The first sentence states the main idea.
The rest of the text explains why clean water is important.
questions.explanation: The main idea is that clean water is important for good health.
misconceptions: Water is used for more than cooking.

questions.stem: Read: 'Kofi was walking home when he saw an old woman struggling with a heavy basket. He stopped to help her carry it. The woman thanked him and gave him a piece of bread. Kofi continued home feeling happy.' What can we learn about Kofi's character?
hints: Kofi stopped to help without being asked.
He carried the basket for the old woman.
questions.explanation: Kofi is kind and helpful because he stopped to help the old woman carry her heavy basket.
misconceptions: Selfish people do not help others.
Unkind people would not stop to help.

questions.stem: Read: 'The farmer looked at his crops and shook his head sadly. The rains had not come for many months. The leaves were yellow and dry.' How did the farmer feel?
hints: He shook his head sadly.
His crops were dry because there was no rain.
questions.explanation: The farmer felt sad and worried because his crops were dying from lack of rain.
misconceptions: The text says he was sad, not angry.

questions.stem: Read: 'The rain started suddenly. The pupils were playing outside. They ran back into the classroom, laughing and shaking off the water.' Why did the pupils run into the classroom?
hints: The rain started suddenly.
They were playing outside when it rained.
questions.explanation: The pupils ran into the classroom to escape the sudden rain.

questions.stem: Read: 'The school library has many books. There are story books, textbooks and picture books. Pupils can borrow books and take them home. There is also a quiet reading corner.' What is the text mainly about?
options: The school library and what it offers
hints: The text describes books, borrowing and a reading corner.
All these are features of a library.
questions.explanation: The text is mainly about the school library and what it offers to pupils.
misconceptions: The football field is not mentioned.
The headteacher's office is not mentioned.

questions.stem: Read: 'Adwoa was very thirsty. She had been playing football under the hot sun. She ran to the tap and drank water quickly.' Why was Adwoa thirsty?
options: She had been playing football in the hot sun
hints: Playing football in the sun makes you sweat and thirsty.
The text says she was playing under the hot sun.
questions.explanation: Adwoa was thirsty because she had been playing football under the hot sun.
misconceptions: Sleeping does not make you thirsty.
Reading does not make you thirsty.
Eating does not make you thirsty in this way.

questions.stem: Read: 'The old man walked slowly with a stick. His back was bent and his hands shook. He smiled at the children as they ran past him.' What can we infer about the old man?
options: He is old and frail but kind
He is angry at the children
hints: He walks slowly with a stick and his hands shake.
He smiled at the children — this shows kindness.
questions.explanation: We can infer that the old man is old and frail (he walks slowly, uses a stick, his hands shake) but kind (he smiled at the children).
misconceptions: He is not young and strong.
He smiled, so he is not angry.
The text does not say he is a teacher.

questions.stem: Read: 'Ama was not feeling well. She had a headache and a fever. Her mother took her to the clinic. The nurse gave her some medicine and told her to rest.' What is the main idea?
options: Ama was sick and got medical help
hints: Ama had a headache and fever.
Her mother took her to the clinic and she got medicine.
questions.explanation: The main idea is that Ama was sick and received medical help at the clinic.
misconceptions: She did not go to school (she was sick).
She did not play with friends.
